sources.label: SPU: Where Does It Go? tool
SPU: How to Sort at Home
SPU: Ban on Batteries and Electronics in Garbage

bins.name: Recycling cart
bins.accepts: Paper, cardboard, bottles, tubs, cans, glass jars

bins.name: Food and yard waste cart
bins.accepts: Food scraps, yard waste, food-soiled paper

bins.name: Garbage cart
bins.accepts: Everything else: no recyclables, food, batteries or electronics

bins.name: Drop-off
bins.accepts: Batteries, electronics, hazardous waste, clothing: not in any cart

prep: Empty it and let it dry
Screw the cap back on
Put it in loose, not in a bag
plastic_bottle.why: Empty, clean plastic bottles and jugs up to 5 gallons are accepted, with the cap attached.

prep: Empty, rinse and let it dry
Only if bigger than 3 inches
Can't get it clean? Garbage
plastic_container.why: Clean, dry tubs, trays and clamshells bigger than 3 inches are accepted; foam containers are not.

prep: Empty and rinse
Labeled "compostable" or "#7 PLA"? Food and yard waste cart
Foam cups go in the garbage
plastic_cup.why: Empty, clean plastic cups are recyclable; dirty cups and foam cups are garbage.

prep: Screw caps back onto the empty bottle
Loose lids must be 3 inches or bigger
Smaller loose caps and lids: garbage
plastic_lid_cap.why: Caps on a bottle and loose lids 3 inches or bigger are recycled; smaller loose ones fall through the sorting equipment.

prep: Keep it out of the recycling cart, even bundled in a bag
Clean, dry film can go to a store drop-off instead
plastic_bag_film.why: Plastic bags and wrap have not been accepted in Seattle recycling carts since January 2020 because they jam sorting machines.

prep: No prep
snack_wrapper.why: Chip bags, candy wrappers and pouches are made of mixed materials that cannot be recycled.

prep: Bag loose packing peanuts and tie the bag
Clean foam blocks: free Special Item Pickup or Styro Recycle in Kent
foam.why: Foam goes in the garbage; only clean Styrofoam blocks have a recycling option.

prep: No prep
Labeled "compostable"? Food and yard waste cart
plastic_utensil_straw.why: Plastic utensils and straws are not recyclable in Seattle.

prep: Keep it clean and dry
Staples can stay in
Shredded paper: food and yard waste cart instead
paper.why: Office paper, mail, newspaper and magazines go in the recycling cart and cannot go in the garbage.

prep: Keep it clean and dry
Stickers, tape and staples are fine
Food-soiled? Food and yard waste cart
paper_bag.why: Clean, dry paper bags are recycled; wet or food-soiled ones are composted.

prep: Flatten it; tape and labels can stay on
Too much for the cart? Box or bundle it beside the cart, no charge
Wet or greasy cardboard: food and yard waste cart
cardboard.why: Clean, flattened cardboard is recyclable; waxed cardboard is garbage.

prep: Remove any foil, plastic or other non-paper pieces
pizza_box.why: Greasy or food-soiled pizza boxes go in the food and yard waste cart.

prep: Napkins, paper towels and uncoated plates with food or grease: compost
Tissues, or towels used with cleaners or bodily fluids: garbage
Shiny coated paper: garbage
soiled_paper.why: Uncoated paper with food or grease on it is compostable, but tissues and shiny-coated paper are not.

prep: Empty it and let it dry
Sleeve can go in too
Labeled "compostable"? Food and yard waste cart
paper_cup.why: Empty, clean and dry paper cups are recyclable in Seattle; foam cups are garbage.

prep: Empty it and let it dry
Leave the spout on; put the cap in the garbage
carton.why: Milk, juice, soup and other aseptic cartons are accepted when clean, empty and dry.

prep: Empty, rinse and let it dry
Push the lid into the can or leave it attached
Leave the label on
metal_can.why: Aluminum and steel food and drink cans are recyclable.

prep: Remove all food and let it dry
Ball it up, bigger than 3 inches
Dirty foil or small bits: garbage
aluminum_foil.why: Clean, dry foil and foil trays larger than 3 inches are recyclable.

prep: Use it up until no contents or pressure remain
Completely empty and non-hazardous (hairspray, cooking spray): recycling cart
Paint, solvents, bear spray or anything partly full: hazardous waste facility, free
aerosol_can.why: Seattle recycles only completely empty, non-hazardous aerosol cans; cans with contents are hazardous waste.

prep: 3 inches or bigger (pots, pans, large lids): recycling cart
Smaller loose pieces: garbage, or a metal can to the transfer station scrap bin
Small lid on its jar or bottle: recycle with it
metal_lid_scrap.why: Metal bigger than 3 inches is recycled; smaller loose pieces fall through the sorting equipment.

prep: Empty, rinse and let it dry
Screw small lids back on; lids 3 inches or bigger can go in loose
No Pyrex or frosted glass
glass_bottle_jar.why: Glass bottles and jars are recyclable; other glass has a different melting point and is not.

prep: Donate whole items in good condition
Broken bottle or jar pieces 3 inches or bigger can go in recycling
drinking_glass_ceramic.why: Drinking glasses, ceramics and other non-bottle glass are not recyclable.

prep: Take off produce stickers and any plastic
Use only approved compostable bags, or none
food_scraps.why: All food, including meat, dairy, bones and shells, goes in the food and yard waste cart.

prep: Cut branches to 4 feet long and 4 inches thick or less
Remove soil
Lid must close, or extra yard waste costs a fee
yard_waste.why: Leaves, grass, plants and small branches go in the food and yard waste cart.

prep: Tape the ends of each battery
Free drop-off at a household hazardous waste facility or city transfer station
Never in the garbage or recycling cart
battery.why: Seattle bans all batteries, even alkaline, from garbage and recycling because they cause fires in trucks and plants.

prep: Donate it if it still works
Take it to a King County Take It Back Network e-cycler
Or book a paid Special Item Pickup
electronics.why: Seattle bans TVs, computers, tablets and anything with a battery from the garbage, though SPU says plain cables and headphones may go in it.

prep: Donate it if it is in good shape
Worn or stained: Threadcycle drop-off at partner thrift stores
Otherwise it may go in the garbage
textile.why: Clothing and fabric can be donated or recycled through Threadcycle, and the garbage is allowed as a last resort.

prep: Donate wearable pairs
Worn out: Threadcycle drop-off at partner thrift stores
Otherwise they may go in the garbage
shoes.why: Shoes can be donated or recycled through Threadcycle, and the garbage is allowed as a last resort.

prep: Make sure it is fully out
cigarette_butt.why: Cigarette butts go in the garbage; vape devices and e-liquid are hazardous waste instead.

prep: No prep
blister_pack.why: Blister packages are hard plastic packaging that cannot be recycled.

prep: Bag it so it cannot tangle
Donate or reuse it if it is still usable
rope_string.why: Rope, twine and yarn with synthetic fibers go in the garbage because they tangle sorting machines.

prep: Ignore any "recyclable" label on the tube
squeezable_tube.why: Soft plastic tubes, like toothpaste tubes, are garbage even when labeled recyclable.

prep: Cut the ear loops on masks first
mask_gloves.why: All face masks, disposable gloves and other protective equipment go in the garbage.
